1 جَذَلَ , (aor.
جَذُلَ , TK,) inf. n. جُذُولٌ, It stood erect, and was firm, (K, TA,) like the جِذْل of a tree. (TA.) And He set himself up as an antagonist to others, in fight. (TA in art. حك.)
And said of a chameleon, It became erect; as also ↓ استجذ . (TA.) You say also, ↓ بَاتَ يَسْتَجْذِلُ عَلَى ظَهْرِ دَابَّتِهِ (tropical:) He slept [during the night] erect, without commotion, upon the back of his beast. (TA.) ＝
-A2- جَذِلَ, (S, K,) aor.
جَذَلَ , (K,) inf. n. جَذَلٌ, (S,) He was, or became, joyful, glad, or happy; as also ↓ اجتذل . (S, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
